Must keep import.meta.dirname-relative fixture paths working (copy or link fixtures, or resolve them from the source tree) and keep stack traces readable with source maps.

  2. BMeasure first, in CIRecommended

    Log per-file time to first result in ci-test.mjs's summary for one week to size the saving on both platforms before choosing A.

  3. CNode's built-in type stripping

    Node 22.18+ strips types natively, but the code imports .js specifiers for .ts files and would need non-erasable syntax removed; not a drop-in.

Impact

Estimate from import timings: ~1.1 s saved per coordinator-importing file (111 files, ~120 CPU-seconds on Linux, roughly three times that on Windows) and most of the contracts suite's 83-105 s; spread across shards, perhaps 1-3 minutes of wall clock per platform. Unverified at suite level.

Risk

A second execution path for tests can diverge from what developers run locally; fixture path resolution and source maps are the likely breakages.

BT-15Install is not the bottleneck; 627 MB of node_modules is one native CLI installed twice on LinuxPerformanceEffort SLow riskMedium confidence
Where
  • package-lock.json:112
  • package-lock.json:125
  • .github/workflows/ci.yml:48
  • packages/adapter-claude/package.json
Evidence
  • ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1 npm ci: 19.8 s wall, 703 MB peak RSS, 622 packages, 338 MB fetched into a partly warm cache; in CI the median is 12 s on Linux and 24 s on Windows (p90 16 s and 29 s). Caching node_modules would save at most ~25 s per job.
  • node_modules is 1.1 GB; 627 MB of it is @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-linux-x64 (316 MB) plus -linux-x64-musl (311 MB). The lockfile entries carry os and cpu but not libc, and npm 10.9's installer checks libc only from package metadata, so the musl build is extracted on glibc runners.
  • npm ci reports 56 audit findings (41 moderate, 14 high, 1 critical); see the dependencies review.
Why it matters

It tells the report what not to recommend: caching node_modules or tuning npm ci buys seconds, while BT-01 to BT-05 buy minutes.

Options
  1. ALeave installation as it isRecommended

    Keep npm ci with setup-node's npm cache; do not add node_modules caching (a ~1 GB restore for a 12-24 s install, plus native-module ABI keys to maintain).

  2. BDrop the musl duplicate

    Check whether a newer npm records libc in package-lock.json (not verified here) and regenerate the lockfile with it; saves ~311 MB of extraction per Linux job.

Impact

A: none, by design. B: a few seconds and 311 MB of disk per Linux job.

Risk

Regenerating the lockfile changes resolved versions unless done carefully (npm install --package-lock-only with the same tree).

No findings in this area match the filters.

Quick wins

  • BT-02 Run npm run lint (3.5 s) as the first step of every test job so a lint-failing push stops within minutes (39 such runs used 5,387 runner-minutes last week); required checks follow once BT-01 cuts the queue.
  • BT-04 Widen descriptor.schema to z.ZodTypeAny before .safeParse in packages/coordinator/test/arke-actions.test.ts:105; excluding that file cut coordinator check time by 22 s (17%).
  • BT-05 Clear the store's 15-second helloFallbackTimer (and reconnect timer) after each client test file; 17 files idle ~15 s each today.
  • BT-06 Make the root build run the client build once plus desktop's esbuild step, and leave the engine's declaration bundle to engine.yml (~76 s of a 91 s step).
  • BT-07 Run tsc through node --max-old-space-size=4096 in the client, desktop and coordinator typecheck scripts so contributors below 16 GB stop hitting heap aborts.
  • BT-12 Add scripts to the oxlint paths in npm run lint (21 ms, 14 errors to fix) and point verify-licenses.mjs at privateDocsRoot().

Keep as they are

Reviewers were asked to name what looks complicated but earns its complexity. These are the parts a simplification effort should leave alone, or change only with the reason in hand.

Coordinator core

emit() as the single event path, with DomainEventSchema validation

Measured at 2.3-31 µs per event (emit-cost.mts). It keeps fold, journal and broadcast consistent. Only the hard-coded policy inside it is worth tabulating (CC-06).

ReadModel as a pure fold (read-model.ts, 545 lines, 79 event cases)

Small, pure and tested (read-model.test.ts). It is not part of the monolith problem.

The StudioServer / StudioServerApplication split and Transport's capability check

Transport authenticates every connection (the CLAUDE.md #825 invariant) and validates each frame once with ClientMessageSchema.parse before dispatch (transport.ts:304), so handlers do not re-validate shape. Any public dispatch must stay in-process.

No concrete harness adapter imports in coordinator.ts

Verified: only a comment names harness/v2-launch.ts. Keep the SPEC-005 §1.1 boundary during the split.

Per-key serialisation of Bench take actions, Bench dispatch and founding decisions

The ordering is deliberate (design turn 180, SPEC-031). Only the implementation is duplicated (CC-11).

Background world store for audiobook and export commands (withBackgroundWorldStore)

Deliberate: these run against a world that may not be the open one. Any router-level world scope (CC-02) must exempt them.

application/ engine layer re-exported as @arke-studio/engine

A public embeddable API with its own policy and operation semantics (#1170). Do not fold it into the Studio router without checking that design.

supervisor.ts

A cohesive generic child supervisor (1,056 lines) with three dedicated test files. Nothing in this review suggests splitting it.

CLIENT_COMMAND_METADATA with compile-time parity (arke-actions/registry.ts)

Reuse its classification and parity pattern rather than duplicating it. Avoid adding a second mapped type over the full 556-kind union, which already costs about 15 s of check time.

The comment density (3,505 comment lines, 14%)

It matches the house style and records why code is shaped as it is. Move comments with their code, verbatim.

Journal flush order and world-ownership checks

CLAUDE.md invariants. Nothing in the plan touches appendFlushed or WorldStore/Committer identity checks.

Production & media pipelines

The outbox protocol in queue/dispatcher.ts (journal submitting before I/O, needs-reconciliation on unknown outcomes, never resubmit on poll noise)

This is the SPEC-009 crash model. Its re-validation after every await is the price of never paying twice; split the file (PM-05), but keep the protocol.

Completed-result receipts (queue/artifact-files.ts)

Hash-verified receipts let a restart land paid output without generating it again. The second write is the cost of that guarantee.

Flushed appends in JobJournal, LedgerFile and ProviderCallStore

This is a CLAUDE.md invariant. Reduce the number of appends (adaptive polling, PM-06), not the flushing.

productionShape as the production-kind capability table

It already centralizes kind behaviour (82 calls, 13 residual raw comparisons). Do not build a second table.

music-render.ts cache design (content key, receipt, in-flight once, chunked loudness that yields every chunk)

The right pattern; PM-12 and PM-14 propose copying it.

ComfyUI digest cache and hashMedia identity memo

Identity-keyed receipts avoid re-hashing multi-GB checkpoints and unchanged takes on every scan.

comic-make-run.ts

An 87-line policy loop over injected operations: the right size and shape for a run loop.

Provider capture and transport seam (capture.ts, transport.ts, http.ts, artifact-body.ts, artifact-transfer.ts)

One wrapper gives every client redaction, bounded downloads and transport diagnostics. It is the real shared client base.

Exact rational spend allocation in spend/rollups.ts (BigInt shares, remainder to the last member)

Prevents micro-dollar drift across pass segments, as the production-spend doc requires.

publishing/ (Aonik resumable upload) and publications/ edition delivery (prepared/promoted/completed phases)

Their complexity matches their failure modes: multipart resume, replacement conflicts, crash-safe promotion.

Per-block chapter-record checkpoint in the audiobook run

SPEC-047 R-18: a stop or a lost claim keeps what was made. PM-02 changes how many commits a checkpoint takes, not whether one happens.

fal submit not being abortable (fal.ts:405-410)

Documented: aborting would discard the request id needed for the remote cancel while the paid job keeps running.

Chat, actions & harnesses

A per-run query lease and a fresh harness session for every World Chat turn

Reads and attachments are scoped to one run and refused after a world switch (#70 §8.2, §9.1); the cost to address is the resent prompt (CH-04), not the isolation.

World content read through leased, paginated target reads with receipts and HMAC cursors

The world is never inlined, so prompts do not grow with canon or sheets, and every citation can be checked against the version and hash it read.

All-or-nothing turn validation with one corrective retry

A reply that refers to propositions that did not persist is worse than no reply (#70 §8.3, §8.4); make it faster and more visible (CH-03), not partial.

WorldChatStore durability: fsync before acknowledging, torn-tail repair and foreign-write refusal

Mirrors the issue 826 flush discipline for the only copy of what was said; CH-06 makes it cheaper without removing a guarantee.

The proposal gate and its ten accept outcomes

Base fingerprints, ripples, rebase, conflicts and open choices each map to a distinct, actionable refusal (explainAcceptRefusal), per SPEC-004; the chat's one-time ripple reconfirmation is a reasoned asymmetry.

The conversation action lifecycle (11 statuses, idempotent execute keyed by action id, recoverPreparation, reconcile, settleFailed)

Needed to recover approved spend and host work after a crash; simplify the per-kind definitions around it (CH-09), not the state machine.

The founding build's immutable authorization record and fsynced journal

Recovery is a fold over record and journal, never a timer; keep it while making publication cheaper (CH-11).

Local setup fetches nothing unasked

All 9 catalogue components are optional (catalogueTotalMb), presence is detected first and disk space is guarded per volume.

Concrete adapter imports only in harness/v2-launch.ts

The #828 decision; the coordinator package intentionally depends on both adapters while Coordinator consumes contracts.

Registry parity over all 556 client commands

Compile-time and runtime checks that every command is classified keep the human-only boundary (approvals, credentials, recovery) explicit at little cost.

Persistence, transport & startup

appendFlushed order (write, fsync, close, acknowledge) for JobJournal, LedgerFile and ProviderCallStore

CLAUDE.md invariant and SPEC-009 §2.2.1; measured at ~0.5 ms per append on Linux it is not the bottleneck - the reads are. Make reads incremental instead.

Strict vs tolerant ledger reads (readAllStrict / readAllChecked)

The distinction prevents duplicate billing rows and dressing an unreadable ledger as empty (SPEC-009 R-16, SPEC-032 R-21); an in-memory index must preserve both behaviours.

World lock heartbeat (20 s), assertOwned disk check per write and the three-failure cutoff

Ownership invariant (issue 827); costs a small file read per write and one utimes per 20 s.

Transport authentication per hello and per media GET, explicit origins, no unauthenticated fallback

CLAUDE.md invariant; timingSafeEqual on a 32-byte token is negligible next to the media gate work in RP-11.

Paged snapshots, 250 ms non-restarting coalescing and SocketWriter bounds with snapshot supersession

Measured field motivation (11 MB snapshots, socket closures on 2026-10-24); ordering keeps events and replaces only waiting snapshots. Build on it rather than replace it.

Scan read-ahead of 16 and the hashMedia identity cache

Measured (2.6 s -> 0.71 s for 3,898 sidecars) and the identity heuristic is the precedent for RP-01 option A.

operationalWrite for conversation and history logs

Introduced to avoid full rescans for app-owned operational writes (issue 1840); the right pattern to extend.

ChangeLog roll at 16 MB with tail-only seq recovery and journalRecord summaries

Bounded a log that reached 2.6 GB (issue 1845).

CoalescedReads for audiobook listening

Prevents a starvation loop observed on 2026-10-24; keep while the underlying read stays expensive.

Launch window before initialization, StartupController failure/retry state

Resolves startup audit ST-1 and the unhandled rejection; option A in RP-10 only moves when initialize() starts, not this structure.

Harness trace synchronous appends and synchronous plan reads in gate preconditions

Documented as rare crash-explaining lines (harness/trace.ts) and as same-disk-truth preconditions (productions/plans.ts:116); not hot.

SystemResourceService on demand with no background timer

Coalesced at 1 s and bounded; only the System panel's 5 s poll drives it.

Child-ledger stale sweep at start-up

Runs a PowerShell/CIM probe only when records remain after a crash; justified by the orphan/file-lock history (startup audit, intentional).

Contracts & dependencies

Zod v3 rather than v4

Measured: v4 classic constructs this kind of schema set 4–6× slower with 4–5× the heap, and v4-mini about 2× slower; with about 36,700 schemas built at import, the parse-speed gain does not pay for it.

Discriminated unions for the 556 commands and 248 events

zod v3 builds a lookup map, so parsing costs one option, not a scan of hundreds; a plain union would be far slower and give worse errors.

Validation of untrusted input at the boundary

Incoming commands (transport and phone gateway) and records read from disk at world scan must stay validated; only re-validation of the coordinator's own output is questioned (CT-03).

Strict write schemas with permissive read paths

Comments in world.ts explain that persisted worlds predate newer write rules; tightening a read schema could stop existing worlds from opening.

Compatibility readers for old scenes, cut.json and V1 package schemas

Worlds on users' disks may still hold those shapes; isolate and rename them (CT-09) but do not delete without a minimum-version policy and a one-time migration.

Feature-gated world schema versions (ensureSchemaVersion)

A deliberate forward-compatibility guard (SPEC-023 R-23); centralise the numbers (CT-15), never renumber them.

valueSchema wrapper

Keeps declaration output bounded so the engine's bundled .d.ts stays within the compiler's limits (TS7056, noted in frames.ts).

Generated INTERACTIVE_PLAYER_SOURCE and AUDIOBOOK_PLAYER_SOURCE strings

The exporters inline the exact player text; a generator and tests keep the copies identical, and as plain string constants they tree-shake out of the client.

three as a contracts dependency

The coordinator and the client must evaluate camera paths identically and the evaluator is versioned; the cost is modest and measured (CT-10).

pdfjs-dist in both client and coordinator

One exact pin and one installed copy serving two jobs: browser preview and the PDF compiler's validator, whose version is part of the compiler identity.

The engine package as a boundary

A thin facade with a pack-install-run CI test and a documented external host; fix its bundle (CT-11), not its existence.

Coordinator's dependency on the concrete adapters, credential policy in harness-env.ts, shared audio contracts in audio.ts

Deliberate invariants recorded in CLAUDE.md (issues #828 and #117); the 2026-08-04 audit's AR-2 was resolved by that decision.

Client state & loading

Module-singleton store read through useSyncExternalStore, with useStoreSelector and shallowEqual

The right primitive: no whole-store React context exists (about 11 small contexts in total). The fix is to use the selector path more, not to replace the store.

shareSnapshot structural sharing, paged snapshots and frame-parser skipping re-validation of the history arrays

Measured cheap (shareSnapshot about 6 ms per MB) and they are what make identity-keyed selectors and caches (CS-01, CS-10) work.

Snapshot and rejoin reset rules, the hello fallback and frameRunRequestEpoch

They encode bugs fixed in review (ids recurring across worlds, holds after a rejoin, quotes surviving a refresh). Move them in a split; do not change them.

The global chat keeping the selected conversation mounted when parked

Preserves drafts and dictation across navigation (issue 2019). Stop it re-rendering while parked rather than unmounting it.

Editor playback writing refs and the DOM each frame and telling React four times a second

playback-engine.ts and editor-transport.tsx already avoid per-frame React renders; it is the pattern for the stage (CS-07 D).

Listener, timer and resource hygiene

Window and document listeners are removed in every file that adds them except main.tsx's app-lifetime drop guards, all 16 intervals are cleared, timers are gated (the System panel samples only while open and visible), object URLs are revoked and every WebGLRenderer is disposed with forceContextLoss.

Hash routing with base './'

Needed for the Electron file page; compatible with lazy chunks, which Vite resolves relative to the importing module.

All CSS imported in main.tsx

Keeps components importable by the node test runner and preserves order-dependent overrides; do not split CSS before introducing cascade layers.

Transport authentication (dev-session handoff, capability never in public HTML, URLs or VITE_* variables)

None of these proposals touch it; lazy chunks and cached hashed assets contain no credentials.

One RouteErrorBoundary per tree, with Settings rendered separately

A broken screen leaves Settings reachable; extend it with a Reload action for chunk-load failures rather than restructuring it.

Screens, components & CSS

CSS imported only from main.tsx, never from components

So the node test runner can import the component graph without a CSS loader (main.tsx:29). Make the order explicit instead of moving imports into components.

BodyLayer, PageSheet, EditorDialog and lib/overlays.ts

Each answers a recorded failure: dialogs clipped by a transformed ancestor (fy-fade-up) and sheets that could not be pressed under a later one. Extend their use; do not replace them.

ResponsiveSheet's portal between inline slot and sheet

It keeps one mounted panel's draft and pending request when the layout switches to a sheet, which two separate renders would lose.

Token files byte-identical to design-system/_ds

A policy-enforced baseline; new tokens (touch target, finer spacing steps) should start in the design system.

Retired-route redirects in App.tsx (ActivityRoute, RetiredDispatchRoute, RetiredSceneChatRoute and 12 Navigate routes)

About 45 lines that keep bookmarks, notification clicks and remedies landing (their comments cite SPEC-014 R-20, SPEC-034 R-5/R-14, SPEC-039 R-1 and SPEC-036 R-37); not dead code.

Composer (9 sites) and ProductionConversation (16 sites)

Successful reuse; bring the two stragglers in (CU-04) rather than redesign.

stage-viewport.ts as an imperative three.js class

A 1,453-line non-React renderer with a narrow interface to SceneStage; splitting it is optional and unrelated to UI duplication.

The fine-grained editor-effect-* modules

34 of the 44 editor modules are imported by tests; keep the granularity and change only where they live (CU-12).

The pure-move method of issue 101 and the issue-1160 cautions

The right way to do CU-07, CU-08 and CU-11: same text at a new path, effect order and keys preserved, no wide hook argument lists, no re-export barrels.

One Loading component and the Working indicator

The decision recorded in loading.tsx is sound; enforce it (CU-13) rather than revisit it.

The smoke-*-layout scripts that compare implementation frames with master frames

They are the guard rails for every CSS change proposed here; running a subset in CI would strengthen them.

check-master.mjs's turn ledger and raw-size ratchet

The model for the ratchets proposed in CU-03, CU-06 and CU-10.

Journey: first run & worldbuilding

Price on the press for the founding build, the look preview and every paid generation

One aggregate authorization stated before spending (SPEC-031 R-13, R-51). This is a deliberate guard on money, not friction to remove.

Begin approves pending founding cards and seeds settled sketches

Avoids asking twice for a decision already given (#2482); the per-sheet approvals it replaced were pure confirmation fatigue.

The proposal gate for anything an agent wrote

Nothing an agent drafted lands without an accept; UJ-03 changes only the case where no agent drafted anything.

Archive is two presses, moves the folder, deletes nothing; a bottom sheet on phones

Reversible and plainly worded; the second press is the consent (design turn 159b).

Discard draft and Reset narrator take a second press

Both destroy a choice or a conversation with uploads; the confirmation lapses on its own.

Phone pairing needs owner approval on the PC, a five-minute single-use code and Tailscale TLS

Security boundary (#825, #1311, SPEC-001 §2.5): keys and pairing controls stay on the trusted desktop.

Settings as a sheet over the remembered screen

Every way into Settings returns the person to where they were (SPEC-042 R-5, R-6).

Six retired settings addresses and the /activity redirect

One line each; they protect bookmarks, persisted remedies and old notification links, and retired-routes.test.tsx guards them.

Onboarding never traps manual authoring

Failed downloads or an unavailable model still allow Start using Arke (onboarding.test.tsx); UJ-06 keeps that, it only makes skipping explicit.

World-open progress labels

A two-minute open used to look like a hang (issue 1844); the phased label is the honest wait.

Launch failure state with Retry, Open data folder and Quit; return to the building screen after a cut-off build

Fixes ST-1 of the 2026-08-04 startup audit and implements SPEC-031 R-33.

Journey: productions & publishing

Prices before money is spent, and a sheet for large runs (Read the book, Plan video's cap and per-pass gates)

Charges are real and sometimes estimated; the sheets name chapters, characters, voices and caps before anything is sent. Simplify where the sheet appears, not whether the price does.

Separate consent before a cloned voice's recording leaves the machine

It is a different question from price (SPEC-022, SPEC-046) and must not be folded into a spend confirmation.

Activity's recovery wording: Resubmit · may charge again, Abandon · prior cost unknown, Try again · no charge

Loss of observation is an unknown outcome, not proof that no charge occurred; the wording keeps people from paying twice by accident (activity-panel.tsx:521-551).

The accept gate for everything Arke drafts (overview, chapters, outlines, episodes, comic plans and scripts)

Nothing lands in the world without a person's accept; every journey here passes through it deliberately.

Accept take is decision and selection in one commit; takes side by side; Reject cites the sheet the take drifted from

SPEC-013 R-9; it keeps one list of choices and makes rejections useful to the next attempt.

Comic page checks (lettering and picture) before Accept, with Accept anyway recorded

Lettering errors are expensive to find after export; the override is explicit and kept on the record.

Export blockers named with a way to clear each (Branch Map's Export blocked · N, comic Go to, audiobook incomplete chapters)

Readiness is shown before the package is made; this is the pattern to spread, not remove.

Publish's capture, preview and Create edition for books, and the immutable edition that results

Editions must be reproducible and recheck their sources; the extra steps buy an edition that cannot silently change.

Submit to Arke Player's frozen edition, hash, explicit rights confirmation and browser sign-in

SPEC-025 R-28 and SPEC-058 R-95 to R-100; host-only, human-only publishing is a deliberate boundary.

The owner's rules: export from a copy of the release import, never replace a published package, never mark a non-app release Latest, ask before any public upload

Pinned phones refuse changed bytes and the Studio's updater reads Latest; automation should enforce these rules, not bypass them.

Retired addresses that still land somewhere sensible

Bookmarks, remedies and Arke links keep working; only the way they are declared should be consolidated (UP-05).

Reviewed creation in the conversational setup (Review production, then Create production)

The plan is visible before anything is written to the world; keep it on the Plan with Arke path even if a Start empty path is added.

Build, tests & CI

Tests on both windows-latest and ubuntu-latest for every push

Windows is the shipped platform and Linux catches path and case assumptions (CLAUDE.md). Windows is two thirds of CI minutes, so the recommendations make it cheaper (BT-01, BT-05, BT-11) rather than rarer.

The ten-minute silence guard and the 30-minute job ceiling

In green run 42343860689 the longest silence any job reported was 47 s (Windows shard 3) and at most 19 s on Linux, and the longest job in 40 green runs was 18.6 minutes, so both limits have headroom; the guard costs nothing and turns hangs into named failures. None of the proposals moves either number.

Node's discovery-based --test-shard and ci-test-plan.test.mjs

No file can fall out of CI. Any change to shard counts or weighting (BT-01, BT-11) should keep discovery as the fallback and keep the coverage test.

The Production Chat film in its own job, skipped by name in the shards

1.4 min on Linux and 2.4 min on Windows at the median; it is the only real-media run of that scenario.

effects.yml and engine.yml with path filters on pull requests

They took ~20 and ~5.5 runner-minutes per run out of every PR; the same policy is the model for BT-01's option B and BT-06.

The custom lint checks (design master, client policy, private docs, player sources)

All eight node steps together take 2.4 s and oxlint 1.1 s for 2,629 files; they are the gate the colour-token rule relies on and are not worth trimming.

Pausing Defender on Windows runners

5-6 s per job; the comment's own condition (keep only if shard times show it pays) has not been re-measured here, but the cost is negligible.

The hand-formatted house style

Keep it; BT-13 only removes the prettier script that contradicts it.

Test hygiene helpers: test/wait.ts until() and test/tmp.ts sweeps

87 coordinator files poll with until() instead of sleeping and every temporary world is swept. The coordinator's remaining fixed sleeps are mostly bounded quiet periods proving that something does not happen (as test/wait.ts explains) or Windows-only timing proofs such as storage/windows-cache-file.test.ts's 15 s admission delay; the avoidable ones are in the client (BT-05).

npm ci per job without node_modules caching

12 s on Linux and 24 s on Windows at the median (BT-15); caching ~1 GB with native modules would add risk for seconds.

Leads to check

Things reviewers noticed but could not confirm. Treat them as questions, not findings.

Coordinator core

  • I probed two of the 57 unguarded handlers that refresh with msg.worldId (rename-world and reorder-episodes). Some of the other 55 mutate through gate or store calls that may validate ids, so each needs checking.
  • I did not run the package's full typecheck (src and test). The coordinator.ts graph alone needed 2.14 GB, which is close to Node's default heap limit here (an earlier traced run ran out of memory at about 2 GB). The CI reviewer should confirm the headroom.
  • I did not audit the 43 raw err.message strings in events individually. Some are deliberate plain-language domain errors; others may carry absolute paths or provider echoes.
  • The 43 per-command *-result and *-refused events are broadcast to every client. Transport already has TransportRequester.reply, used only for the Studio assistant, so per-requester replies may be possible. That needs a client and multi-window review before anyone relies on it.
  • It is unverified whether the Studio's prose commands (create-production, create-chapter, save-chapter) could route through the application/ engine services that packages/engine exposes (issue #1170, SPEC-025 context).
  • The spend pass cost is unmeasured with real job rows (larger than the fixtures, with landed files and finalization), with Bench event files, and on Windows with Defender.
  • I did not measure AppSettingsFile per-read cost on Windows, or check whether any other process writes settings.json while the app runs.
  • The responsibility map classifies by name. Roughly 5% of units may be assigned to the wrong domain: for example, export-cut is counted under exports, and read-aloud methods under audiobook.

Production & media pipelines

  • local-ai/verified-loopback-http.ts with windows-connection-origin.ts: every managed-Ollama or Studio-writer request appears to spawn a PowerShell verifier plus a PowerShell leash helper (job-leash.ts:280), and the code notes CI exhausting a 12 s budget. The per-request overhead on Windows is probably 0.5-1.5 s but was not measured. A long-lived verifier could amortize it; check SPEC-061.
  • providers/src/clients/artifact-body.ts:29-50 keeps every chunk and then copies them into one buffer, so peak memory is about twice the artifact size (the default limit is 1 GiB per file). Preallocating from Content-Length, or streaming to the receipt file, would halve it.
  • Start-up runs removeFiled for every historical succeeded job (dispatcher.ts:2394), and each call lstats a receipt directory: O(history) syscalls. Limit it to jobs with unsettled finalization, or keep a marker.
  • A completed fal job's result JSON is fetched twice, once by poll and once by fetchArtifacts (fal.ts:455-458 and 475-483); one cached body would save a round trip per job.
  • Submission storage admission (mkdir, root acquisition, reservation assessment, inside the world lock) runs twice per submission (dispatcher.ts:1063 and :1324). Its cost on Windows, and whether the StorageMonitor reading is reused, was not measured.
  • Whether the lane slot should be held during the remote poll phase for cloud async providers, and fal's actual account concurrency limit, were not verified (PM-06 option B).
  • prepareBook prepares chapters sequentially and re-hashes each cloned voice clip once per chapter, because the referenceOf cache is per chapter (audiobook-run.ts:415).
  • spend/rollups.ts:61 and :162 search all jobs once for every Bench take without a jobId: O(Bench takes × jobs) per production-spend pass.
  • The ComfyUI client listens on a progress WebSocket but still GETs /queue on every poll (comfyui.ts:928-929); completion could be event-driven with a slow fallback poll.
  • Every world gateOp and ownedWrite ends with a full scanWorld, even when changed paths are known (world/store.ts:272-283). This is the root of PM-02 and PM-03's commit cost and belongs to the persistence reviewer.

Chat, actions & harnesses

  • Possible race: the send handler publishes the transcript (coordinator.ts:8700-8701) as soon as sendNow returns, while the runner may not yet have appended turn.started (run.ts:796); onAdmitted (run.ts:800) emits only a send result, so the user's line may be missing from the published transcript until completion unless the client shows it optimistically. Not traced in the client.
  • World Chat's own appends (turn.started, turn.completed, run.finished, renames) are not wrapped in ownedWrite or operationalWrite, unlike the input journal (input-journal.ts:215-222), and WorldChatService.load writes checkpoint.json from unguarded callers (conversation-authoring.ts:47, conversation-inputs.ts validView). Check against issue #827 whether ownership loss should fence them.
  • Target reads rebuild all rows and hash whole collections (conversationActionDigest over all canon, sheets or reference kits) on every page (target-reads.ts:132-183, 1150-1209), so paging a large target is O(pages × size); not measured on a large world.
  • The local-GPU wrapper calls adapter.listModels() on every default-model send (harness/local-gpu.ts:50); whether OpenCode caches that catalogue was not verified.
  • On the Claude engine every World Chat turn starts a new Agent SDK query (a Claude Code subprocess) in a fresh run scratch folder; the adapter notes Claude Code keeps one transcript per working directory under ~/.claude/projects/, so each turn likely leaves a new folder there. Not measured.
  • Local setup's detect() asks Ollama for its model list once per pull entry (four entries, local-setup.ts:739-742), and installs strictly one component at a time in catalogue order (local-setup.ts:768-801, 873-899), so small voice models wait behind multi-gigabyte runtimes; memoising the list and starting small independent components first would shorten time to first use. Benefit not measured.
  • Prefix caching across the per-turn sessions (OpenCode, Claude, Codex, Ollama) was not measured; CH-04 option B's gain depends on it.
  • compactSettledStageReviews runs on every refreshConversations (three times per turn) and reads the whole changes.jsonl when any stage review exists (productions/stage-review.ts:85-109); owned by the production-pipelines review.
  • openWorldChat also projects human decisions by reading plan records for productions (world-chat/human-decisions.ts) on each of its 3–4 calls per turn; cost not measured.

Persistence, transport & startup

  • Real record sizes: synthetic journal rows were ~1.45 KB with 6 rows per job and artifact prompts 2.7 KB; real distributions (finalization, landing, speech quotes) may be larger or smaller and change all history-proportional numbers linearly.
  • If the newest 2,000 provider-call records exceed 50 MB, ProviderCallStore compacts on every write (three per call) - code-read only.
  • productionSpend receipts are part of every snapshot barrier; their size for video-heavy productions was not measured.
  • Windows costs (Defender scan on open, FlushFileBuffers latency, where.exe and icacls spawn time) were not measured; the Windows impact estimates rely on code comments and the 2026-08-04 audit.
  • The gain from starting initialize() before first paint (RP-10 A) is unmeasured; it depends on renderer bundle parse time on the target machine.
  • WorldChatStore.append re-reads, parses and hashes the whole conversation log per append (world-chat/store.ts:246-262) - same pattern as RP-02, owned by the chat reviewer.
  • The storage inventory walk (every 5 minutes, up to 250,000 lstat calls per root) may be costly on large model folders; not measured.
  • scan.ts mediaHashCache is a module-level map never evicted across worlds; entries are small, so likely harmless.
  • Reconnect frequency of real phones over Tailscale (and therefore the real cost of RP-08) is unknown.
  • Client-side cost of applying a 17 MB first snapshot is outside this slice (client loading reviewer).

Contracts & dependencies

  • Real snapshot sizes for a large world were not measured, so the share of coordinator and client CPU spent in snapshot validation (CT-03) is extrapolated from a 315 KB synthetic snapshot.
  • Phone and browser timings are inferred: Node/V8 in this container stands in for Chromium on desktop, and a phone is assumed to be several times slower.
  • In Vite dev the browser fetches the 251 contracts modules individually on each load; adding the linked package to optimizeDeps.include might speed development reloads but was not measured and may hurt edits to contracts.
  • productionExportFingerprint sorts keys and ids with host-locale localeCompare; ULIDs and slugs make a difference between hosts unlikely, but a phone computing it with its own ICU and locale against the desktop's was not tested.
  • Whether any third-party code calls detached methods on the app's zod v3 schemas (relevant to CT-02 A) was not audited, and the full test suite was not run against the patched zod build.
  • The coordinator defines 147 more z.object schemas in 66 files; some may duplicate contracts shapes; not reviewed.
  • 62 contracts modules (932 public values, 21,218 lines) serve only the coordinator; moving server-only prompt and model-guide modules into the coordinator might clarify ownership. In the client bundle they total 182 KB, mostly events.ts and world-chat-actions.ts reached through FrameSchema.
  • The client's trackEndFrame (picture-edit.ts:177) shares a name but not semantics with the contracts function of the same name (it ignores a track's endFrame); possibly a latent inconsistency.
  • adapter-claude, adapter-opencode and providers' higgsfield-cli each carry about 30-line runCommand, resolveOnPath and versionOf helpers; not compared line by line.

Client state & loading

  • Per-item selector subscriptions at mount: the 2,000-tile Artifacts mount went from about 320 ms to 426-480 ms after switching Portrait to a selector, in a noisy shared container; confirm before choosing CS-02 A or B.
  • Style recalculation cost of the 1.29 MB global stylesheet on large DOMs such as the Artifacts shelf was not measured.
  • Lazy chunks on the sandboxed Electron file page under the current CSP were not run here; expected to work because the entry is already a module script loaded from file://.
  • Whether Tailscale Serve compresses responses was not checked; the phone figures assume it does not.
  • Real event rates in busy sessions (jobs, audiobook runs, world open) are unknown; per-second costs assume 1-10 events per second plus up to 4 snapshots.
  • WorldChatView's early return before useConversationInputs (world-chat.tsx:762, 780) was not reproduced; its parents appear to unmount it first.
  • Evaluating the contracts barrel took 258-308 ms in Node 22 (a 2.19 MB esbuild bundle) while the whole app's script time to first screen in Chrome was 96 ms; the browser share of contracts was not isolated (contracts reviewer).
  • React 19.2.8's Activity component for the parked chat unmounts effects while hidden; whether dictation and send holds survive that needs a spike.
  • React Compiler feasibility after the Rules-of-Hooks clean-up was not tried.
  • After CS-01 A, about 26 renders per event remain on the world overview from always-mounted components that still call useStore() (AppChrome, QueueToaster, ActivityPanel, SystemPanel, SessionRefusal, UpdateAnnouncement, GlobalChatProvider).

Screens, components & CSS

  • RemoteVoiceUploadConfirmation's position: fixed overlay is mounted in place at 12 sites rather than through BodyLayer; under an ancestor that still carries the fy-fade-up transform it would be clipped, as testing.md describes for other dialogs. Not reproduced, since the app was not run.
  • 152 :has() selectors, including .fy-app:has(.fy-production-setup) at season-responsive.css:78 and :227, may add style-recalculation cost on large DOMs; not measured.
  • App.tsx imports every screen eagerly and SceneStage statically imports three.js (stage-viewport.ts:45); only story-pdf-preview uses a dynamic import. three.js and all 1.45 MB of CSS are therefore likely in the start-up bundle, for the loading-performance review to confirm with a build.
  • Voice choosing is drawn at least three ways (VoicePickerDialog, the character voice catalogue sheet at character-voice.tsx:940, the audiobook narrator list); they may share one list and preview row, but SPEC-046 R-37 and design 176 may intend the differences. Not assessed.
  • build-review.mjs lists 482 of 612 screens as drawn and not built, with hand-maintained statuses and dates; some may be stale against the code. Not cross-checked.
  • Six launch tokens (--launch-bar-fade, --launch-bar-quiet, --launch-flare-core, --launch-flare-haze, --launch-flare-mid, --launch-panel-bg-muted) have no var() use in client CSS or TSX; they may be kept on purpose with the turn-158 record.
  • 127 raw <img> elements in 65 files and 26 onError fallbacks in 17 files suggest a shared media-image component could replace ad-hoc hiding logic; not analysed.
  • chapter-timing.tsx's usePeaks decodes audio in the browser while Audio Studio and music use coordinator-provided waveforms; possibly two waveform paths for the same need, not traced.
  • design-system/ is 503 tracked files and about 127 MB (PNG 81 MB, HTML 36 MB including the 15.7 MB master) in every clone; Git LFS for bitmaps could shorten checkouts. For the build and CI review.

Journey: productions & publishing

  • In the running client the Develop page appears to show a production outline canvas while the conversation sits in the global panel (conversation.tsx:861-862, global-chat.tsx:59-66); not observed running, and the SSR tests render the older full-page layout.
  • The cost of one whole-book audiobook door preparation, and so the real load from the rail's asks during writing, was not measured; coordinator timing or app.jsonl entries would settle it.
  • The retired exports address sends books, comics and music to cut?export=1; what the Cut shows for a production without scenes was not checked.
  • A comic's CBZ, PDF and EPUB files seem not to be listed anywhere after the export dialog closes (the web-package kinds enum has no comic file kind); the coordinator's merged listing was not read in full.

Build, tests & CI

  • The concurrent-job ceiling of 20 is inferred from running jobs plateauing at 20 for 40 hours of the week (one 39-job instant during a mass cancellation looks like an accounting artifact); the account's plan was not checked.
  • Windows causes for the worst-ratio suites (flushed appends, WorldStore index builds, fixture copies) are hypotheses; nothing was profiled on a Windows runner.
  • TypeScript 7's speed (34.9 s for the combined Node program) was measured on a contended 4-vCPU VM with 6.5 GB peak RSS; behaviour on 16 GB Windows runners and in editors was not checked.
  • Savings from widening registry.ts:1746 and onboarding.ts are estimated from trace spans; only the arke-actions test cost was measured by exclusion.
  • Whether a newer npm records libc in the lockfile (dropping the 311 MB musl build) was not verified.
  • The desktop main bundle (built here into scratch in 1.3 s) is 17.9 MB unminified and includes three.js (0.53 MB) and undici (2.1 MB) through contracts and the coordinator; relevant to the desktop-startup review, not measured at runtime.
  • The recurring other-workspaces failure signature (60 runs over the week, 8 on main) traced to two client tests on 11-01; whether later recurrences were the same tests or flakes was not checked.
  • Agent PR volume (304 branches in a week) drives CI demand; whether drafts or batched pushes could cut runs further depends on how the sessions are orchestrated, which was not examined.

Method and limits

Ten reviewers ran in parallel against commit 42d3def (v0.5.116) on 7 November 2026. Each had one slice of the system and the same brief: find options for simpler code, faster software and shorter journeys; tie every finding to files and lines; offer options with trade-offs; and name what should stay as it is. Seven worked from source and git history. Three measured: the runtime reviewer ran benchmarks against the real coordinator code on synthetic worlds, the client-state reviewer counted re-renders by mounting the real App and timed it in headless Chrome, and the build reviewer installed dependencies, measured the bundle, type-checking, lint and sample tests, and read one week of CI history through the GitHub API.

All local measurements come from a Linux container with 4 CPUs and 16 GB of memory, shared with the other reviewers while they ran, not the Windows machines the app ships to and not the CI runners. Treat absolute times as indicative and the ratios as the useful part. Several Windows-specific costs (process spawns, Defender, icacls) are named but not measured.

The private specification set was not available. About 3,200 SPEC citations sit in package source. Reviewers were told never to infer what a cited requirement says. Findings that touch cited behaviour list the citation and carry lower confidence; treat them as questions for whoever owns that specification.

The journey reviewers read routes, navigation calls, buttons and on-screen strings without running the app. Their step counts describe what the code allows, not observed sessions.

Some behaviour was out of bounds for every reviewer: the journals' flush order, the world-ownership checks and heartbeat cutoff, transport authentication, the harness import rule and the shared audio contracts. Several findings make those paths cheaper, with fewer reads around a flush or fewer rescans around an ownership check. None removes one.

Before publishing, all 1,003 file-and-line references across the 139 findings were checked mechanically against the commit, and every code line quoted in evidence was checked to exist verbatim in the repository. One line range (CT-12) pointed four lines past the end of a 41-line file and was corrected. One reference into zod's own source under node_modules stays as evidence but cannot be linked.

The claims the summary leans on were then re-checked by hand:

  • CC-01: handleClientMessageInner spans packages/coordinator/src/coordinator.ts:7683 to line 21828, and its switch holds 564 case lines (the 556 command kinds plus a few nested cases).
  • CC-02: rename-world renames whichever world is open without comparing ids, then refreshWorldSnapshot loads the world named in the message.
  • CC-08: 438 of 1,504 main-line commits since 9 August touched coordinator.ts (29.1%).
  • RP-01: there are 131 gateOp call sites and only 2 pass finalWrite: "commit".
  • CH-01: ownedWrite rescans unconditionally after every call.
  • CH-05: promptReserveTokens is declared in the adapter contract and implemented by no adapter, so the documented 64,000-token cap no longer applies.
  • PM-02: the repository's own Windows filing profile shows three full scans per block, 367 ms per block at zero artifacts and 1.29 s at 3,750.
  • RP-04: the jobs and ledger tables rebuilt at start-up are read only by two methods with no callers.
  • RP-05: desktop main builds the studio host in-process, so the coordinator shares Electron's main thread.
  • UJ-01 and UJ-02: only cast/:sheetId/edit is routed, and the Factions page's only New button is hidden at 1100px and wider.
  • CU-02: the Propose-timing hook's propose and accept are never called from product code.
  • CS-03: BookRequests calls useProductionReading on the right of a short-circuit, so the hook disappears when the connection drops.
  • CS-04: the remote gateway sets Cache-Control: no-store on every response, and nothing compresses.
  • CT-01: the contracts manifest has no sideEffects field and no exports map.
  • BT-04: packages/coordinator/test/arke-actions.test.ts:105 calls safeParse on a union of every action's schema.
  • BT-05: the client store's hello fallback is a 15-second setTimeout that nothing clears between test files.
  • BT-10: the providers, voice and desktop tsconfigs include only src, so about 13,600 lines of their tests are never type-checked.

None of these checks failed.
